$comment: HAND-EDITED source of which settings an agent may change (MCP settings_set and settings_reset, the socket's cli/mcp/script/remote writers; plans/cmux-next/settings-react.md section 3), one file per key: <key>.json is {agent, why?}, so two pull requests that each add a setting add two files and never touch the same line (cmuxterm-hq docs/rfd/drafts/conflict-free-tests-deploy.md). Every key of the schema has exactly one file, with no default: scripts/cmux-next/gen-settings-sources.py fails on a row with no file, so a new setting cannot reach agents without a decision. agent is settable (an agent may set and reset the key: looks and layout, usually) or the refusal that says why not (one of refusals below); why is the reason, the same text on every key it covers. The settings schema export writes agent_settable and agent_refusal per row from it; gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift copy the app enforces at its one write path (SettingsSchema+AgentPolicy.generated.swift: SettingsSchema.agentSettableKeys, agentRefusedKeys, SettingWriter).

refusals.doc: The key decides what leaves the machine or what is recorded.
The key opens network access or egress.
The key can end terminals or other work.
The person decides it; agents do not, in v1 (picker.pinned: which folders the picker offers first).
